item.title: Trump administration reverses stance on integration of people with disabilities
item.description: Disability rights advocates are angered by the latest reversal but are rallying behind proposed legislation and working with states to strengthen protections for community integration.

item.title: Studying this super El Niño could save lives. NOAA is scaling back research
item.description: A powerful El Niño is already influencing extreme weather around the planet. During the last strong El Niño, federal agencies ramped up research in the hope of improving weather forecasts. This year, they won't be matching that effort.
item.content:encoded:

item.description: The FAA's ambitious overhaul of the air traffic control system comes amid rising public anxiety about AI. The CEO of the company that's building the software explains how it works.

item.title: SNAP's funding model is starting to change. Here's what that means for the program
item.description: States will start to pay a larger share of the bill to run the food assistance program, as federal funding for operational costs shrinks.

item.title: Egg prices have tumbled since Trump returned to office. Here's why
item.description: Agriculture experts say high egg prices were the result of severe avian flu outbreaks, but the Trump administration's tariffs and the war with Iran have also put pressure on farmers.

item.title: Tennessee governor halts executions after Christa Gail Pike survives lethal injection
item.description: Tennessee officials were unable to put Christa Gail Pike to death Wednesday for a 1995 murder after administering two doses of a lethal drug. Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee halted the remaining execution for the year.

item.title: Police questioning can shape a sexual assault case. Their approach is often wrong
item.description: The Cornell lawsuit filed by a woman alleging a brutal rape raises questions on how police handle such cases. The majority of police lack adequate training on trauma-informed approaches, experts say.
